hook: A massive machine just carved a tunnel 65 meters beneath the Panama Canal.

sections.voiceover: A massive machine just carved a tunnel 65 meters beneath the Panama Canal.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of the Herrenknecht Mixshield TBM cutterhead rotating slowly.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep mechanical grinding sound building in intensity.
b_roll: Archives of Herrenknecht Mixshield TBM cutterhead
Stock footage of Panama Canal water surface

sections.voiceover: On October 26, 2026, the 13.46-meter wide TBM named Panamá completed its 4.5-kilometer drive. How much earth did it move to reach Albrook station?
sections.visual_cue: Animated map showing the Panama Metro Line 3 path under the canal.
b_roll: Animated map of Panama Metro Line 3 route

sections.voiceover: The excavation resulted in a massive 700,000 cubic meters of rock and soil removed.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the excavated material volume represented by an infographic.
b_roll: Stock footage of tunnel spoil removal

sections.voiceover: To stabilize the tunnel, the team installed 2,295 concrete rings along the path. Peak performance reached 300 meters per month during the project.
sections.visual_cue: Time-lapse style animation of concrete segments fitting into a ring.
sections.sfx_cue: Metallic clicking of segments locking together.
b_roll: Animation of precast concrete ring assembly
Herrenknecht technical footage of segment installation

sections.voiceover: This breakthrough officially connects the metro line beneath the Panama Canal.
sections.visual_cue: Final breakthrough shot at the construction site.
